lines.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; render MISMATCH. The cap is the registered ambiguity amb.2025.refund_cap_5d: i1040gi p. 90, worksheet line 1, 'But don't enter more than the amount of your state and local income taxes shown on your 2024 Schedule A, line 5d'; line 5d is the total of 5a, 5b and 5c, and the project chose the cap as printed (line 5d), the reply the income tax part. The exceptions the reply names are not omitted: 1 ('a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024') and 5 ('You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025') refuse at refund.not_prior_year (remedy: Pub. 525), and 2 ('a refund other than an income tax refund') is now computed by Pub. 525 Worksheet 2 (rec, refund.taxable), as i1040gi p. 89 directs; line 1's own refusals are only those the worksheet itself raises (refund.exc_tax, refund.exc_who).

Ruling: representation; render UNCLEAR. The four helpers are defined lines rendered by label (refund.amt_you_born, amt_you_blind, amt_spouse_born, amt_spouse_blind: $1,550 or $1,950 per box checked), so line 6 is 'Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)'. The married-filing-separately condition of the worksheet footnote ('you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return', i1040gi p. 90) is in the spouse-box questions themselves (refund.spouse_born, refund.spouse_blind); a 2024 qualifying surviving spouse return has no spouse on it, so its spouse boxes are zero (refund.spouse_boxes; amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024).
